QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_59

question.text: Under SAS-1100 a common DOUBLE-COUNTING risk is:

answer.text: Counting CSR-donor funds and ZCZP-bond funds for the same unit as two separate sources of impact

explanation.text: The Logic: A housing unit funded partly by CSR donors and partly by ZCZP-bond proceeds can be reported by both the CSR donor's impact statement and the SE's Annual Impact Report on the SSE. If neither side de-duplicates, the same unit is counted twice in aggregate impact figures. Good data-analysis practice requires the SIA to remove duplicate entries and clarify funding-source attribution so each impact unit is attributed once. The Trap: Options B, C and D — counting rent, donations, or votes — are not relevant double-counting risks in SE impact assessment. Note: The cited SIA workbook discusses CSR, DIB/ZCZP/SSE funding routes and the general data-analysis instruction to remove duplicate entries, but does not specifically identify the CSR-donor + ZCZP-bond double-attribution scenario at the per-unit level. The framing above reflects general impact-accounting practice rather than a workbook-page citation.
